slots.practicalActivity: Draw your own Order-to-Cash flow diagram (order -> fulfillment/shipping -> billing -> cash application -> GL), labeling which Oracle Fusion module and which role (sales admin, warehouse, billing analyst, cash applier) owns each stage. Then open Order Management and Receivables in your practice environment and map each work area to a stage on your diagram.
slots.deliverable: Your own labeled O2C flow diagram plus a short map of practice-environment work areas to each stage.

slots.practicalActivity: In your practice environment, open Manage Customers and review an existing customer account's bill-to/ship-to sites and price list assignment the way the lesson reviews Harborview Industrial Supply's setup. Then write your own transaction plan listing the documents you expect to create across Chapters 2-5 (order, shipment, invoice, receipt) before creating any of them.
slots.deliverable: Notes on the real customer setup you reviewed, plus your own written document plan for the transaction you'll run.

slots.practicalActivity: Create your own sales order the way SO-48217 is built: select a customer account, confirm or override bill-to/ship-to, add a line with an item and quantity, set a requested ship date, and submit it.
slots.deliverable: One submitted sales order in your practice environment with customer, line, and ship date confirmed.

slots.practicalActivity: Review how your Slot 3 order's line was priced from the customer's price list and whether a discount applied. Then check whether it was flagged for a credit check or hold the way SO-48217 was for its size, and if so, walk it through release.
slots.deliverable: Your order's pricing breakdown (list price, discount if any) plus a note on any hold it triggered and how it was released.

slots.practicalActivity: Make a real change to your submitted order (increase the quantity or change the ship-to site) and process it as a formal order change. Then practice cancelling a line on a second, throwaway order to see which statuses allow cancellation and which don't.
slots.deliverable: One order with a processed change recorded, plus notes on which line statuses blocked cancellation on your second order.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: without referring back to the lessons, create a second sales order end to end for a different item and quantity -- select the customer, confirm sites, add the line, let it price, set a ship date, submit, and resolve any hold it triggers. Time yourself and note any step you had to look up.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently created and submitted sales order, plus a short self-assessment of which step needed a lookup.

slots.practicalActivity: Follow your submitted order into the warehouse side: review how Order Management releases a line to a pick slip, and walk through the pick, pack, and ship sequence for your order's line the way the lesson lays it out for the 400 control panels.
slots.deliverable: A written or system record of your order's line moving through pick, pack, and ship steps.

slots.practicalActivity: Confirm the shipment for your order's line (recording ship date and quantity shipped). Then create a Return Material Authorization for a partial quantity of a different, already-shipped order the way the lesson processes a damaged-units return, and note how the RMA affects inventory and the pending invoice.
slots.deliverable: One confirmed shipment plus one processed RMA with its effect on inventory/billing noted.

slots.practicalActivity: Walk your shipped order's line to the billing work area, confirm it's eligible to invoice, and interface it to Receivables, tracking it through the same staging step the lesson describes for SO-48217's line before AutoInvoice runs.
slots.deliverable: Your order's line shown staged for AutoInvoice, with the invoicing-eligibility and interface steps recorded.

slots.practicalActivity: Run AutoInvoice against your staged line and resolve any rejection or error it produces (for example a missing remit-to address) using Manage AutoInvoice Lines. Then issue a credit memo against your Slot 8 RMA's returned units.
slots.deliverable: A successfully created Receivables transaction from AutoInvoice after resolving any error, plus one credit memo tied to your return.

lessons.title: The Receivable and the Cash Receipt

slots.practicalActivity: Review the open receivable your invoice created, then enter a cash receipt for the customer and apply it to that specific transaction, confirming the open balance clears (or is reduced correctly, if your credit memo also applies).
slots.deliverable: One applied cash receipt against your receivable, with the resulting open balance recorded.

slots.practicalActivity: Drill your invoice's and receipt's accounting (revenue/receivable at invoice, cash/receivable at receipt) into the General Ledger, confirming both journals landed on the accounts you expected.
slots.deliverable: A short writeup of the two journals (invoice and cash receipt) with their GL accounts confirmed.

slots.practicalActivity: Perform your own AR-trial-balance-to-GL reconciliation on this transaction (and, if you still have an open balance from the RMA/credit memo, check that too), confirming every checkpoint from order through cash ties out.
slots.deliverable: A reconciliation memo confirming your transaction's checkpoints (order, shipment, invoice, receipt, GL) all tie out.

slots.practicalActivity: Replay your entire transaction end to end in one sitting, listing every document number and journal in order the way lesson 23 replays SO-48217. Then pick one exception scenario (a credit hold, a short-shipped line, an AutoInvoice rejection) and resolve it on a new order.
slots.deliverable: A one-page document/journal chain for your transaction plus one resolved exception scenario.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately break one checkpoint in a brand-new transaction (for example, ship a different quantity than was ordered, or leave a new customer site without a remit-to address) and troubleshoot it back to its source, documenting each diagnostic step.
slots.deliverable: A troubleshooting log for one deliberately broken transaction, from symptom to root cause to fix.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can run a complete Order-to-Cash cycle in Oracle Fusion Cloud -- from sales order through fulfillment, AutoInvoice, cash application, and GL reconciliation -- and troubleshoot a break at any checkpoint.
